analysis.investment_thesis: Angel One grew spectacularly from 440 Cr revenue (FY17) to 5,239 Cr (FY25) on the retail trading boom, but FY26 shows the fragility: revenue fell to 5,137 Cr and net profit crashed 22% YoY to 915 Cr as SEBI's F&O restrictions bite. With 28.87% promoter holding and borrowings spiking to 7,951 Cr, this is a business in structural transition — not a safe entry.
key_strengths: Exceptional historical growth engine: revenue CAGR 31.4% and net profit CAGR 45.7% over 9 years on the back of India's retail investor explosion
Gross margins of 84.78% reflect the capital-light, tech-first brokerage model with strong brand in Tier 2/3 cities
Forward P/E of ~20x reflects market pricing in recovery — if SEBI headwinds ease, earnings can rebound
key_risks: Net profit fell from 1,172 Cr to 915 Cr in FY26 — first earnings decline in a decade, driven by SEBI F&O curbs that crushed derivative volumes
Borrowings exploded from 788 Cr (FY23) to 7,951 Cr (FY26) to fund margin trading book — D/E now 0.76, above the 0.6 red-flag threshold
OCF only positive 2/5 years; FY26 OCF was deeply negative at -4,142 Cr — massive working capital consumption
red_flags: Promoter holding only 28.87% — far below the 50% minimum; management has very low skin in the game
Borrowings up 10x in 3 years (788 Cr → 7,951 Cr) while profits decline — dangerous leverage trajectory
Market cap 29,375 Cr with declining earnings is the worst combination for a SMILE investor
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Angel One is a victim of its own success story colliding with regulatory reality. The business built a dominant retail brokerage franchise via technology and was among the key beneficiaries of India's D-Mat account explosion (100M+ accounts). But SEBI's crackdown on F&O trading — which drove a disproportionate share of brokerage revenues — has exposed the earnings fragility. FY26 profit of 915 Cr is the lowest since FY23 despite a much larger balance sheet.

The structural concern beyond regulation is the balance sheet: borrowings have grown from 788 Cr to 7,951 Cr in three years to fund the margin funding book, making Angel One increasingly look like an NBFC with brokerage income rather than a capital-light technology broker. Finance costs tripled to 437 Cr in FY26. For a SMILE investor, the low promoter holding (28.87%) is the dealbreaker — management does not have sufficient alignment with minority shareholders during this turbulent transition.
